name: ICICI Bank Ltd
title: ICICI Bank Ltd - 532174 - Transcript Of The Call With Media And Of Earnings Call With Analysts And Investors

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 PBT ex-treasury up 10.1% to ₹18,209 crore on provisions of just ₹96 crore (0.03% of advances), but guidance is only "range-bound" NIMs and no loan or deposit growth numbers; the provision drop is partly one-off recoveries.

summary.headline: ICICI Bank Q4 FY26 PBT ex-treasury rose 10.1% YoY to ₹18,209 crore, with provisions falling to just ₹96 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 profit before tax excluding treasury grew 10.1% YoY to ₹18,209 crore and profit after tax grew 8.5% to ₹13,702 crore, helped by provisions of only ₹96 crore versus ₹891 crore in Q3. Core operating profit grew only 5.1% YoY as operating expenses rose 12.0%, so the bottom line leaned on low credit costs and recoveries from written-off accounts. Loan growth accelerated to 15.8% YoY, led by rural (+25.6%), business banking (+24.4%) and mortgages (+13.2%), while deposits grew 11.4%. Management declined to guide on loan growth and said NIM should stay range-bound in FY27, while flagging West Asia conflict uncertainty without yet seeing portfolio stress.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.30% in Q3 FY26; FY26 NIM 4.32%, similar to FY25
vs ₹891 crore in Q3 FY26 and ₹891 crore in Q4 FY25 per call; about 90% YoY decline
vs loss of ₹157 crore in Q3 FY26 and gain of ₹239 crore in Q4 FY25
vs 0.37% at Dec 2025 and 0.39% at Mar 2025

segments.name: Retail loans
segments.commentary: Retail portfolio grew 9.5% YoY and 4.2% QoQ, 41.7% of total portfolio including non-fund. Mortgages +13.2% YoY, personal loans +7.2%, auto loans +1.7%, credit cards -5.6% YoY and -1.3% QoQ.

segments.name: Rural (incl. gold loans)
segments.commentary: Rural portfolio grew 25.6% YoY and 18.0% QoQ, driven by higher gold loan demand and expanded branch machinery.

segments.name: Business banking
segments.commentary: Business banking grew 24.4% YoY and 7.6% QoQ; management said it has held up through COVID, the 2022 energy shock and tariffs.

segments.name: Domestic corporate
segments.commentary: Domestic corporate loans grew 9.3% YoY and 3.1% QoQ; corporate is about 20% of the book. 71.9% of corporate book rated A and above.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: ICICI Life VNB rose to ₹26.29 bn in FY26 (margin 24.7% vs 22.8%); ICICI General combined ratio 103.4%; ICICI AMC PAT ₹7.63 bn in Q4.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to be range-bound in FY27, unlikely to move up, per management.
Management gave no loan growth target; said deposit growth will not constrain loan growth (LCR about 126%).
Management aims for operating expense growth below top-line growth, though it does not target a cost-to-income ratio.
Credit cost was 38 bps in FY26 and under 50 bps when adjusted for the agri standard asset provision and corporate recoveries; management expects a healthy trend line but gave no FY27 number.
Management expects some GDP impact in FY27 from West Asia conflict, depending on duration.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 7,511 at March 31, 2026, after 126 openings in Q4 and 528 in FY26.
ATM and cash recycler network at 12,087.
Contingency provisions held at ₹13,100 crore (about 0.9% of advances), not utilised.
Standard asset provision of ₹1,283 crore on agri priority sector held per RBI direction; bank still working through the portfolio to bring it into conformity with agri classification.
demand_pricing: Competitive environment; management says pricing must balance good-quality customers with fair pricing.
Average current and savings deposits grew 11.3% YoY; government SA balances are a low-teens share of SA balances.
Treasury loss reflected RBI guideline capping onshore FX net open positions.
Credit card book contracted for a second quarter; management cited revolver decline and a focus on profitable segments.
Mortgage pickup attributed to better disbursements after benchmark stabilised, not lower prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 8.5% PAT growth came from low provisions versus core income?
qa_highlights.answer: Core operating profit grew 5.1% in Q4 and 7.7% in FY26; provisions fell about 89-90% YoY and PBT ex-treasury grew about 10%. Management said treasury was little changed.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit rates rise, given recent falls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate direction depends on macro conditions and it is difficult to make a long-term call; the bank focuses on CASA and primary-banking relationships.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the mortgage pickup and does the deposit-loan gap persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage growth reflects benchmark stability and better disbursements. Average deposit growth (about 10.8%) is close to average loan growth, and LCR is about 125-126%, so deposits will not constrain loans.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any provision release or write-back this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower retail net additions, moderating unsecured slippages, and higher corporate recoveries including recoveries from written-off accounts drove the low provisions. Contingency and agri standard asset provisions were not used.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sub-50 bps credit cost sustainable into FY27, given the West Asia conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is difficult to forecast given the lack of clarity, and it will focus on good-quality customers and monitor developments. It sees no cause for concern in retail, and business banking is being monitored.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the credit card business and its market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Card book fell 5.6% YoY; management attributed the decline to spends and revolver levels, exited riskier segments, and said profitability remains healthy. It gave no market share figure.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: supply shocks, energy prices, and corporate and MSME stress, with management saying it is too early to call and the Dubai and Bahrain presence being monitored.
Provisions at ₹96 crore are unlikely to be repeated; they were helped by one-off corporate recoveries from written-off accounts, so credit cost normalisation is a risk.
Core operating profit growth of 5.1% and opex growth of 12.0% show negative jaws in Q4; management wants opex growth below income growth.
Deposit repricing and NIM range-bound outlook as cost of deposits falls; government SA balances in low-teens share of SA balances.
Co-lending book: management declined to give NPA ratio separately, and the portfolio is under ₹1,500 crore in retail plus SME, described as early-stage.
Agri priority sector provisions of ₹1,283 crore are still held and under review, with an update expected in about one quarter.
Pending regulatory items: CIC reporting moving to fortnightly; treasury impact from FX position caps.
summary.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet, liquidity, capital and asset quality, but cautious and frequently non-committal on FY27 outlook, citing West Asia uncertainty. Management repeatedly declined to give growth, NIM or segment-mix targets, and deflected the Iran payments and forex-loss questions.
key_quotes: So, given this scenario, we look at risks, we look at profitability, we look at good quality customers and what falls within our framework, we will continue to grow within that area.
We do expect NIMs to be range-bound in FY27.
We do not give any specific targets for going forward.
So, definitely, we would want to have opex growth at a level which is below the top line growth.

adds.what: Branch network at 7,511 at March 31, 2026 (126 openings in Q4, 528 in FY26)
ATM and cash recycler network at 12,087

growth.why: Management gave no loan growth target and only said NIM will be range-bound in FY27 and opex growth will stay below top-line growth; no specific capacity or orders back any growth, with branch openings the only concrete items.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM was 4.32% in Q4 (vs 4.30% in Q3) and FY26 was similar to FY25, with management guiding range-bound NIM in FY27; cost of deposits fell to 4.43% from 4.55%, but core operating profit grew only 5.1% against 12.0% opex growth.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network reached 7,511 after 126 openings in Q4 and 528 in FY26, and ATM/cash recycler network is 12,087, so the branch expansion is running at a steady pace, though no capacity plan or capex figure was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Loan growth accelerated to 15.8% YoY with rural +25.6%, business banking +24.4% and mortgages +13.2%, though no loan growth target was given and credit cards shrank 5.6% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no loan growth target and said NIM will be range-bound and unlikely to move up in FY27, with West Asia uncertainty limiting any upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 provisions of ₹96 crore are unlikely to repeat (Q3 was ₹891 crore), and management said West Asia could hit FY27 GDP, so credit cost normalisation could pressure the 38 bps FY26 credit cost.

rows.label: Opex growth below top-line growth
rows.why: Opex rose 12.0% YoY in Q4 against core operating profit growth of 5.1%, and management wants opex growth below income growth, though it gave no cost-to-income target.

rows.label: Agri standard asset provision update
rows.why: ₹1,283 crore of agri priority sector standard asset provision is still held per RBI direction, and an update is expected in about one quarter, which could release or require provisions.

rows.label: West Asia conflict impact on portfolio
rows.why: Management expects some GDP impact in FY27 depending on duration, and business banking and corporate/MSME stress is being monitored, with domestic corporate at 20% of the book and 71.9% rated A and above.

tone.note: Management was confident on capital (CET-1 16.35%), liquidity (LCR about 126%) and asset quality (GNPA 1.4%, NNPA 0.33%), but was non-committal on FY27 loan growth, NIM and credit cost given West Asia uncertainty; analysts pressed on how sustainable the sub-50 bps credit cost is and on the card book
